guide.what: SquachWatch, TalkingSasquach's surveillance-device detector for the ESP32 "Cheap Yellow Display", ported to the FREE-WILi 2. Its own firmware runs unmodified; it watches the FREE-WILi 2's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scans for Flock cameras, ALPR readers, body cams, Flipper Zeros and the like.
guide.see: Squachy's walkthrough (a tap moves it on), then a card for your time zone, then the main screen. Nothing is in range until you add something below.

tryit.label: Tap through the walkthrough
tryit.text: - nine taps, 2.5 s apart. Then pick your zone with > and press THIS IS RIGHT.

tryit.label: Ordinary networks nearby
tryit.text: - two Wi-Fi networks and a pair of earbuds: nothing to flag.

tryit.label: A Flock camera appears
tryit.text: - within a scan or two SquachWatch raises its alert. Tap the card to dismiss it.

tryit.label: Walk into town
tryit.text: - a small town's worth of cameras, a WiFi Pineapple and a Flipper.
The colour buttons press the button bar: grey SCAN, yellow LOG, green DESK (keys 1, 2 and 3). Hold HOME 5 s to leave.
The stock scans give network names, hardware prefixes and Bluetooth names only, so trackers found by their advert data (AirTags, Tile, Remote ID) aren't detected yet.

guide.check: The log shows each scan ([fw2] Wi-Fi scan N: ...) and "squachwatch: screen ALERT" when something is found. Detections are logged to the SD card, which lives in memory here.
